_meta.description: Complete feed mill library — formulation guidelines, process parameters, QC targets and troubleshooting
sources: NRC 2001/NASEM 2021 Nutrient Requirements of Dairy Cattle

units.energy: kcal/kg ME (poultry/swine) or MJ/kg NE (equine) or Mcal/kg NEL (dairy)

calcium_pct_dm.note: Low Ca pre-calving to prevent milk fever

nsc_pct.note: Non-structural carbohydrates — critical for insulin-resistant horses

de_mcal_day.note: 1.4-1.9x maintenance DE depending on workload intensity

electrolytes.note: Sodium, potassium, chloride supplementation required for heavy sweat loss

copper_mg_kg.note: Sheep very sensitive to copper toxicity
Goats more tolerant than sheep but still sensitive

ddgs.variability: HIGH — nutrient content varies by source and processing

key_limits.poultry: Max 15% finisher, 8% starter/grower — high sulphur and variability
key_limits.swine: Max 25% finisher, 20% grower — reduce lysine digestibility adjustment
key_limits.dairy: Max 15-20% DM — watch sulphur and mycotoxins

key_limits.poultry: Max 12% finisher, 8% starter — glucosinolates in non-00 varieties
key_limits.dairy: Excellent bypass protein source — up to 15% DM
key_limits.beef: Good protein source up to 12% DM

key_limits.swine: Avoid in breeding stock — gossypol reproductive effects
key_limits.beef: Max 15% — gossypol tolerance higher than monogastrics

key_limits.swine: Max 5% — banned in EU for ruminants
key_limits.ruminants: BANNED in most countries for BSE risk

watch_for: banned in ruminant feed in most countries

key_limits.poultry: Max 5% starter, 3% grower/finisher — tainting risk above 3%
key_limits.swine: Max 6% early weaner, 3% grower — taint and cost

_meta.description: Feed mill process parameters, equipment settings and QC targets

grain_moisture_max_pct.note: Above these levels — dry before storage or risk of mould

receiving_and_storage.aflatoxin_screening: Every load from high-risk origins (Africa, South Asia, South America during wet seasons)

roller_mill.note: Roller mills produce more uniform particle size than hammer mills — preferred for swine

micro_ingredient_addition.note: Micro ingredients must be pre-mixed or added via premix — never add direct at <0.1% inclusion

batching_and_mixing.sequence: Add dry ingredients → mix 30s → add liquids → mix to target time → discharge

conditioning.note: Higher temperature = better pellet quality but destroys heat-sensitive additives (vitamins, enzymes, probiotics)

die_specifications.die_material: X46Cr13 stainless for standard; X90CrMoV18 for abrasive ingredients

temperature_out_c.note: Pellet temp at discharge should be ≤8°C above ambient

cooling.note: Insufficient cooling = moisture condensation = mould risk. Over-cooling = excessive moisture loss = shrinkage

crumbling.note: Crumble after cooling — never before. Check roll wear weekly

sampling_frequency.incoming_raw_materials: Every load — moisture, visual, mycotoxin screening
sampling_frequency.finished_feed: Every batch — moisture, pellet quality, weight
sampling_frequency.quarterly: Full nutrient analysis vs formulation target

moisture_limits_pct.note: Below 11% = excessive dry matter loss (cost). Above 13.5% = mould risk

nutrient_analysis_tolerance.note: Finished feed analysis should be within these tolerances of the formulation target

pellet_length_uniformity.note: Oversized pellets cause feed wastage in poultry — adjust knife settings

bagging_and_dispatch.batch_traceability: Batch number, date, formulation code, raw material lot numbers — minimum 12 month retention

_meta.description: Feed mill troubleshooting guide — symptom to causes to solutions
_meta.use: Match user-reported symptom to closest entry. Provide top 3 causes and solutions.

poor_pellet_durability.symptom: PDI below target, pellets break easily, crumble on handling

causes.detail: Below 75°C — insufficient starch gelatinisation
Less than 20 seconds retention — steam not penetrating
Fat >5% acts as lubricant — reduces pellet binding
Low L/D = insufficient compression = weak pellets
Worn/enlarged holes reduce compression
Large particles create weak points in pellet matrix
High fibre/protein formulations bind poorly
Insufficient steam addition

solutions: Increase conditioning temperature to 80-85°C
Increase steam pressure to 3.5-4.0 bar
Increase retention time in conditioner — reduce throughput
Add pellet binder (lignosulphonate 0.5-1.0%, bentonite 1-2%)
Check and replace worn die
Reduce fat addition — move fat to post-pellet application
Reduce hammer mill screen size for finer grind
Check steam quality — ensure dry saturated steam not wet steam

high_fines.symptom: Excessive fines/dust in finished pellet, fines >5% poultry or >3% swine

causes.detail: See poor_pellet_durability entry
Roll gap too tight for crumbled products
Smooth rolls cannot grip pellets — crush rather than crumble
Too many transfer points, bucket elevators, pneumatic conveying
Rapid cooling creates surface micro-cracks

causes.cause: Sieve screen damage or wrong size
causes.detail: Fines not being removed before bagging
Hot pellets soft — mechanical damage during conveying

solutions: Address root pellet quality issues first
Increase crumbler roll gap — reduce aggression
Replace worn crumbler rolls
Minimize conveying distances and transfer points
Check and repair sieve screens
Ensure pellets cooled to ≤8°C above ambient before conveying
Apply molasses or liquid fat post-pellet (1-2%) to bind fines
Recycle fines back to conditioner — max 5% of batch

pellets_too_long.symptom: Inconsistent pellet length, many oversized pellets

causes.detail: Blunt knife or wrong knife angle
Pellet extrudes too far before cutting
Fast extrusion before knife can cut
Insufficient conditioning or formulation issue

solutions: Sharpen or replace cutting knife
Adjust knife gap — 1-2mm from die face
Reduce die speed if variable
Check conditioning — improve pellet hardness at exit

low_throughput.symptom: Mill producing below rated capacity, slow production rate

causes.detail: Blocked holes reduce effective die area
Poor roll-to-die contact
High fibre, low starch, high fat formulation
Steam pressure too low or temperature too low

causes.cause: Feed rate to conditioner not matched to press
causes.detail: Inconsistent feed flow
Drive motor at maximum — reduce feed rate

solutions: Check and clean blocked die holes
Adjust roll-to-die gap — typically 0.1-0.3mm
Review formulation — reduce fat, increase starch
Increase steam pressure and conditioning temperature
Calibrate feeder for consistent flow rate
Check main drive motor and gearbox condition
Consider die with larger hole count or different L/D ratio

press_blockage.symptom: Pellet press chokes and stops, feed builds up

causes.detail: Wet feed masses and blocks die
Feed too wet to pass through die
Cold die — fat congeals and blocks holes
Metal, stones, string blocking die holes
Different pelleting characteristics without die adjustment

solutions: Check steam trap — ensure dry saturated steam
Reduce moisture addition — check steam pressure
Pre-warm die with oilseed meal before pelleting
Check and repair magnets and stone traps
Never overfill conditioner — control feed rate
When restarting after blockage — use oilseed meal to clear die
Install pressure relief on conditioner

high_energy_consumption.symptom: Power consumption per tonne above normal (>35 kWh/tonne typical pellet)

causes.detail: Worn die holes increase resistance
Too tight gap increases friction
Fibrous ingredients require more energy to pellet
Un-gelatinised starch harder to compress
Slipping rolls waste energy

solutions: Replace worn die and rolls
Optimise roll gap — 0.1-0.3mm from die
Improve conditioning — more steam, higher temperature
Review formulation — high fibre increases energy demand
Check and tighten drive belts/couplings

high_shrinkage.symptom: Finished product weight significantly less than raw material input, shrinkage >1.5% above expected

causes.detail: Grain/ingredients above 14% moisture — more water to evaporate
Cooler running too long or too much airflow — excessive moisture loss

causes.cause: High moisture addition in conditioner losing in cooler
causes.detail: Steam moisture added then removed in cooling — net loss
Counter-flow cooler set too slow — over-cooling
Dry weather increases evaporation from product

solutions: Monitor and control incoming grain moisture — reject above 14%
Calibrate cooler airflow — target ≤8°C above ambient at exit
Measure shrinkage by weighing batches — track daily
Reduce cooler retention time if over-drying
Add moisture post-cooling if legal and within specification
Target finished product moisture 11.5-12.5% to minimise shrinkage while maintaining safety

high_moisture_finished_product.symptom: Finished feed moisture above 13.5% — mould risk, rejected loads

causes.detail: Pellets not cooled enough before bagging
Insufficient air volume to remove moisture
Humid weather — cooling air itself humid
Condensation inside bags

causes.cause: Too much moisture added in conditioning
causes.detail: Steam addition too high for cooler capacity
Production rate exceeds cooler capacity

solutions: Increase cooler retention time — reduce production rate
Check cooler fan and airflow — clean filters
Check discharge temperature — must be ≤8°C above ambient
Do not bag product above specification — recycle through cooler
Reduce steam addition in conditioner
In humid weather — run cooler longer or reduce throughput

mould_in_finished_feed.symptom: Visible mould growth, musty smell, customer complaints

causes.detail: Above 13.5% — supports mould growth
Condensation in bags
Mouldy grain in — mouldy feed out
High humidity or temperature in warehouse
Propionic acid/organic acid below effective level

solutions: Check and correct finished feed moisture immediately
Screen all incoming raw materials — reject mouldy lots
Add mould inhibitor — propionic acid 0.1-0.3%, or organic acid blend
Check warehouse conditions — max 15°C, max 65% RH
Implement FIFO — first in first out stock rotation
Clean bins and silos regularly — mould biofilms persist
Check mycotoxin levels in suspect materials

feed_segregation.symptom: Fine particles and coarse particles separate in bins/feeders — inconsistent nutrient delivery

causes.cause: Wide particle size distribution in mash
causes.detail: Mix of very fine and very coarse particles

causes.cause: Vibration during transport or bin filling
causes.detail: Fines migrate to centre, coarse to edge
Dense minerals settle to bottom
Different particle sizes and densities

solutions: Pellet instead of mash to eliminate segregation
Reduce particle size variation — tighter hammer mill screen specification
Ensure premix properly incorporated — adequate mixing time
Add molasses 0.5-1.0% as binder to reduce dust and segregation
Review bin design — mass flow vs funnel flow

poor_feed_palatability.symptom: Animals refusing feed, reduced intake, lower than expected performance

causes.detail: Fat/oil added without antioxidant — especially in hot climates
Even sub-visible mould reduces palatability
Canola >15%, cottonseed, rapeseed above limits
Too high or too low sodium
Maillard reaction from excessive conditioning temp
Fish meal above 3% — fishy taint
Particle size or texture not appropriate

solutions: Add antioxidant to all fat-containing feeds — BHT/BHA 100-200g/tonne or vitamin E
Screen raw materials for mycotoxins — add mycotoxin binder
Check ingredient inclusion rates — reduce bitter ingredients
Verify salt level against formulation
Reduce conditioning temperature if >90°C
Reduce fish meal inclusion or switch to white fish meal
Add flavour enhancer for problem cases — butyric acid, betaine, molasses

die_maintenance.new_die_startup: Run oilseed meal (soya/canola) through new die first — conditions die holes and prevents blocking
die_maintenance.shutdown_procedure: Always push through oilseed meal at end of production — prevents fat congealing in holes
cleaning_blocked_die: Use drill to clear individual holes
